heading: Injection: Tac
body: Tac accepts the same annotations in its browser services, with two differences. First, Lifetime is a literal object, not a string. {"value":"prototype"} gives every component instance its own service. {"value":"singleton"} is the default and shares one service. A service with NeedsAll already has one instance for each component, because it takes its component's properties. NeedsAll follows Lombok's RequiredArgsConstructor: every field without an initial value is required, and a field with an initial value is plain state. A required collaborator is injected, and every other required field must come from the component's props. The build refuses a page that does not pass one, and the browser refuses a missing or null value. So a required field and a Needs field are never null when a method runs, and the build refuses one that is declared nullable with TY1331. Write the language's non-null form: `open!: boolean` in TypeScript, `late final String path;` in Dart, `val path: String` or `lateinit var path: String` in Kotlin, `let path: String` in Swift (or `var store: Store!` for a Needs field), `public required string Path;` in C#, and `path: String` in Rust instead of `Option<String>`. A field that may stay empty is plain state: give it a starting value, such as `note: string | null = null`. `ty migrate fix --write` rewrites the simple cases. A required field whose name is the instance name of a service, such as documentation next to DocumentationService, is that service and never a prop. So the build also refuses a page that passes :documentation to that component, with TY1407: rename the field, for example to documents, to receive the value, or mark it Needs and stop passing it if you meant the service. Lifetime is for a service like CartService, which keeps state for each component without those properties. Second, Needs finds a Tac provider from the field name in lowerCamel case. So CartService declares cartPricesHelper and cartHelper. A field that copies the class name, such as `CartPricesHelper`, stops the build with TY1332, because an injected field uses the language's variable case. It writes no constructor at all. AuditService calls its field ledger, so it gives the provider's name with Named("CartPricesHelper") instead. Only JavaScript, TypeScript and Dart appear below, because only browser services have a graph of injected services. Dart marks each injected field final, and it also writes no constructor. A native companion accepts Service, Lifetime and NeedsAll, but the source code that it prepares for its native build has no graph of injected services. So a Swift, Kotlin, C# or Rust tab here would show something that the compiler does not do. A required field in a Swift or Kotlin companion can be a let or val with no value. Tachyon writes the constructor for it and fills the field from the props. A Go web service has no graph of injected services either. Java, F# and Ruby services cannot use Helper at all: the build refuses it in those languages with TY1308. An entity Store is the exception: it has no dependencies and opens the context of its own Setup, so a service in every Tac language asks for one with Needs, and an F# service takes it as a constructor parameter (see Data access: Tac). A Converter is the other exception: it has no dependencies and needs no context, so a service asks for it the same way (see Mapping: Tac). Roles: Tac above shows where native roles go.
